See N4 Lesson 21-3's はずだ for a related but weaker expectation. On a certainty scale: に違いない (very confident, near-certain conviction) sits above はずだ (a reasoned, likely expectation), which in turn sits above かもしれない (a mere possibility) — see N4 Lesson 7 for that lower end of the same scale.

18.title: 〜に比べて
18.explanation: Used to compare two or more things, highlighting the differences between them.

examples.jp: 今年の夏は去年に比べて涼しい。
examples.en: This summer is cooler compared to last year.

examples.jp: 田舎は都会に比べて物価が安い。
examples.en: Prices are cheaper in the countryside compared to the city.

18.summary: に比べて sets up a direct comparison between two things, highlighting how they differ.
18.details:
今年の夏は去年**に比べて**涼しい。 *(This summer is cooler compared to last year.)*
田舎は都会**に比べて**物価が安い。 *(Prices are cheaper in the countryside compared to the city.)*

に比べて is a neutral, straightforward comparison marker — compare with より (used in the よりほうが comparative pattern, N5 Lesson 12-3), which structures a comparison around choosing/preferring one option; に比べて simply states how two things differ, without necessarily framing one as better.

18.title: 〜わけだ
18.meaning: That's why ~ / So it means ~ / No wonder ~
18.structure: Plain form (な-adj + な／N + の) + わけだ
18.explanation: Expresses a natural conclusion drawn from known facts, or a restatement that makes sense of the situation.

examples.jp: 彼は十年日本に住んでいる。日本語が上手なわけだ。
examples.en: He has lived in Japan for ten years. No wonder his Japanese is good.

examples.jp: 一時間に二本ということは、三十分に一本のわけだ。
examples.en: Two per hour means one every thirty minutes.

18.summary: わけだ marks a logical conclusion or a satisfied realization that things add up.
18.details:
十年住んでいる。日本語が**上手なわけだ**。 *(Ten years there: no wonder he's good.)*

Often with なるほど. The reasoning is in the facts already given. Contrast with はずだ, which predicts something from an expectation.

18.title: 〜わけがない
18.structure: Plain form (な-adj + な／N + の) + わけがない
18.explanation: A strong denial: the speaker is convinced something cannot be true.

examples.jp: あんな高い車を、学生が買えるわけがない。
examples.en: There's no way a student can buy such an expensive car.

examples.jp: 彼が嘘をつくわけがない。
examples.en: He would never lie.

18.summary: わけがない states that something is impossible, based on the speaker's strong conviction.
18.details:
あんな高い車を、学生が**買えるわけがない**。 *(A student can't possibly buy a car like that.)*

It expresses subjective certainty, sometimes with emotion. Related: はずがない (same meaning, a bit more logical in tone).

18.title: 〜わけにはいかない
18.structure: V dictionary form / V ない-form + わけにはいかない
18.explanation: Social or moral circumstances make it impossible to do (or not do) something, although one might want to.

examples.jp: 明日は試験だから、遊びに行くわけにはいかない。
examples.en: I have an exam tomorrow, so I can't go out to play.

examples.jp: お世話になった人の頼みは、断るわけにはいかない。
examples.en: I can't refuse the request of someone who has helped me.

18.summary: わけにはいかない says 'I can't' for reasons of duty, etiquette or circumstance, not ability.
18.details:
明日は試験だから、**遊びに行くわけにはいかない**。 *(I can't go out; I have an exam.)*

With the negative form, it means 'must': 行かないわけにはいかない = I have no choice but to go. Not used for physical inability.

18.title: 〜ようがない
18.meaning: There is no way to ~ / Cannot possibly ~
18.structure: V ます-stem + ようがない
18.explanation: Says that no method exists to do something, usually because of missing information or tools.

examples.jp: 連絡先が分からないので、連絡しようがない。
examples.en: I don't know the contact info, so there's no way to reach them.

examples.jp: ここまで壊れてしまっては、直しようがない。
examples.en: Now that it's this broken, it can't be fixed.

18.summary: ようがない means 'no way to ~': the means are lacking rather than the will.
18.details:
連絡先が分からないので、**連絡しようがない**。 *(Without their contact details, there's no way to reach them.)*

The preceding verb is in ます-stem. Similar to できない but focused on lacking the means (説明のしようがない = indescribable).

19.title: 〜として（は）／〜としても／〜としての
19.meaning: From the viewpoint of / As for / In the capacity of
19.structure: Noun + として（は）／としても／としての + Noun
19.explanation: Indicates the standpoint, capacity, or role of someone or something. 'としては' emphasizes the standpoint. 'としても' means 'also as'. 'としての' modifies a following noun.

examples.jp: 彼は教師としては素晴らしいが、親としてはどうだろうか。
examples.en: As a teacher he is wonderful, but I wonder about him as a parent.

examples.jp: 趣味としても、スポーツは良いものだ。
examples.en: Even as a hobby, sports are a good thing.

examples.jp: 社長としての責任を果たす。
examples.en: I will fulfill my responsibilities as the company president.

19.summary: として branches into three related forms here: としては (emphasizing a standpoint), としても (also/even as), and としての (modifying a following noun).
19.details:
### The として Family

| Form | Role | Example |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **としては** | Emphasizes a specific standpoint | 彼は教師**としては**素晴らしいが、親としてはどうだろうか。 |
| **としても** | Also/even in the capacity of | 趣味**としても**、スポーツは良いものだ。 |
| **としての** | Modifies a following noun | 社長**としての**責任を果たす。 |

All three build on the base として (role/capacity) — としては often sets up an implicit comparison between two roles (as a teacher... vs as a parent...), while としての simply lets として attach before a noun instead of standing at the end of a clause.

19.title: 〜はもちろん／〜はもとより
19.structure: Noun + はもちろん（のこと）／はもとより
19.explanation: Used to state that the first item is obvious, and then to add another, often more surprising or extreme, item to it. 'はもとより' is more formal.

examples.jp: 彼は英語はもちろん、フランス語も話せる。
examples.en: He can speak French, not to mention English.

examples.jp: 結果はもとより、その過程も重要だ。
examples.en: The process is important, let alone the result.

19.summary: はもちろん／はもとより states that the first item is obviously true, then adds a further, often more surprising, item on top of it — 'not to mention X, Y too.'
19.details:
彼は英語**はもちろん**、フランス語も話せる。 *(Not to mention English, he can also speak French.)*
結果**はもとより**、その過程も重要だ。 *(The result goes without saying — the process matters too.)*

The first item (英語, 結果) is treated as an obvious given; the second item, marked with も, is the point actually being emphasized as also true, often more noteworthy. はもとより is the more formal written equivalent of はもちろん — both share the same underlying "needless to say X, and Y as well" logic.

19.title: 〜ずにはいられない
19.structure: V ない-form (drop ない) + ずにはいられない
19.explanation: An action is so natural or the emotion so strong that one cannot hold back.

examples.jp: その話を聞いて、笑わずにはいられなかった。
examples.en: Hearing that story, I couldn't help laughing.

examples.jp: おいしそうな匂いがして、食べずにはいられない。
examples.en: It smells so good I can't resist eating.

19.summary: ずにはいられない expresses an irresistible urge to act, unlike simple inability.
19.details:
その話を聞いて、**笑わずにはいられなかった**。 *(I couldn't help laughing at the story.)*

する becomes せずにはいられない. The pattern describes feelings that act on the speaker; ないではいられない is the more colloquial variant.

19.title: 〜ような気がする
19.meaning: I feel as if ~ / I have a feeling that ~
19.structure: Plain form / N の + ような気がする
19.explanation: A vague, intuitive impression that cannot be backed up with evidence.

examples.jp: どこかで彼に会ったような気がする。
examples.en: I feel like I've met him somewhere.

examples.jp: 今日はいいことがありそうな気がする。
examples.en: I have a feeling something good will happen today.

19.summary: ような気がする marks a subjective hunch rather than a verified fact.
19.details:
どこかで**会ったような気がする**。 *(I feel as though we've met somewhere.)*

The speaker softens a claim to an impression. Use 気がする as the standard 'sense' predicate; 〜という気がする is slightly more affirmative.

19.title: 〜ように見える
19.structure: Plain form / N の + ように見える
19.explanation: Describes how something appears based on its look or the visible situation.

examples.jp: 彼は疲れているように見える。
examples.en: He looks tired.

examples.jp: この絵は写真のように見える。
examples.en: This painting looks like a photograph.

19.summary: ように見える reports an appearance-based impression, leaving open whether it is accurate.
19.details:
彼は**疲れているように見える**。 *(He looks like he's tired.)*

It focuses on the visible look, unlike らしい (based on information) and ようだ (general inference). 見える can be replaced with 思える for a more mental impression.

19.title: 〜とみえる
19.structure: Plain form + とみえる／とみえて
19.explanation: A literary inference from visible clues: it looks as though ~, judging by what is seen.

examples.jp: 地面が濡れている。夜のうちに雨が降ったとみえる。
examples.en: The ground is wet. It seems it rained during the night.

examples.jp: 彼女は余程うれしかったとみえて、一日中笑っていた。
examples.en: She seems to have been very happy, as she smiled all day.

19.summary: とみえる infers a cause from observed signs, in a written style.
19.details:
地面が濡れている。**雨が降ったとみえる**。 *(The ground is wet; it must have rained.)*

とみえて links the inferred cause to an observed result (〜とみえて、〜). It belongs to formal prose and is less common in speech.

20.title: 〜を通して／〜を通じて
20.structure: Noun + を通して／を通じて (をとおして / をつうじて)
20.explanation: Has two meanings: 1) To do something 'through' an intermediary (a person, experience, medium). 2) A state continuing 'throughout' a period of time.

examples.jp: インターネットを通して、世界中の人と友達になれる。
examples.en: Through the internet, you can become friends with people all over the world.

examples.jp: この地域は一年を通じて暖かい。
examples.en: This region is warm throughout the year.

20.summary: を通して／を通じて covers two related meanings: doing something 'through' an intermediary, and a state persisting 'throughout' a period of time.
20.details:
### Two Meanings of を通して／を通じて

| Meaning | Example |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Through an intermediary** (person, medium, experience) | インターネット**を通して**、世界中の人と友達になれる。 |
| **Throughout a period** of time | この地域は一年**を通じて**暖かい。 |

The two forms are largely interchangeable in most contexts, though を通じて leans slightly more toward the "throughout a time period" reading and formal/written register, while を通して is common in both senses in everyday speech.

20.title: 〜とともに
20.structure: Noun / Verb (Dictionary form) + とともに
20.explanation: Has two meanings: 1) Doing something 'together with' someone/something else (similar to と一緒に). 2) As one thing changes, another thing changes 'along with' it.

examples.jp: 家族とともに、海外へ引っ越すことになった。
examples.en: I am going to move overseas together with my family.

examples.jp: 年をとるとともに、体力が落ちてきた。
examples.en: Along with getting older, my physical strength has declined.

20.summary: とともに covers two meanings: doing something together with someone/something, and one change happening alongside another.
20.details:
### Two Meanings of とともに

| Meaning | Example |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Together with** (similar to と一緒に) | 家族**とともに**、海外へ引っ越すことになった。 |
| **Along with** (as one thing changes, so does another) | 年をとる**とともに**、体力が落ちてきた。 |

The "together with" meaning is a more formal/written alternative to と一緒に. The "as X changes, Y changes too" meaning parallels N4 Lesson 10-6's 〜ば〜ほど (both track a paired change), though とともに doesn't require repeating the same verb/adjective the way ば〜ほど does.

20.title: 〜ようとする
20.explanation: Describes an attempt to do something (not necessarily successful), or an action on the verge of starting.

examples.jp: 彼は窓から逃げようとした。
examples.en: He tried to escape through the window.

examples.jp: 家を出ようとしたとき、電話が鳴った。
examples.en: Just as I was about to leave the house, the phone rang.

20.summary: ようとする covers a deliberate attempt or the moment just before an action begins.
20.details:
彼は**窓から逃げようとした**。 *(He tried to flee through the window.)*

Unlike てみる (try and see), ようとする emphasizes effort toward a goal that may fail. With とき it means 'about to ~'.

20.title: 〜ようとしない
20.meaning: Won't even try to ~ / Refuses to ~
20.structure: V volitional form + としない
20.explanation: The subject shows no willingness to make the effort. It is a criticism of someone's attitude.

examples.jp: 息子は自分で片付けようとしない。
examples.en: My son won't even try to tidy up by himself.

examples.jp: 彼は謝ろうとしなかった。
examples.en: He wouldn't even try to apologize.

20.summary: ようとしない says someone doesn't make any move to do something, often with blame.
20.details:
息子は**自分で片付けようとしない**。 *(My son makes no attempt to tidy up himself.)*

The subject is normally a third person. For the speaker's own refusal use たくない or 〜ない.

20.title: 〜ふりをする
20.structure: Plain form / N の + ふりをする
20.explanation: Describes acting in a way that gives a false impression, such as pretending to sleep or not to know.

examples.jp: 彼は寝たふりをして、私の話を聞いていた。
examples.en: He pretended to be asleep and listened to what I said.

examples.jp: 知らないふりをするのはやめて。
examples.en: Stop pretending you don't know.

20.summary: ふりをする means feigning a state or action; the pretense is deliberate.
20.details:
彼は**寝たふりをして**、私の話を聞いていた。 *(He feigned sleep.)*

Unlike つもり (a self-held belief), ふり is for the impression given to others. The plain-form verb before ふり can be present or past.

20.title: 〜つもりだった／〜つもりで
20.meaning: Was going to ~ (but didn't) / With the intention of ~
20.structure: V dictionary form + つもりだった／つもりで
20.explanation: つもりだった talks about a past intention that did not come about. つもりで marks the purpose or mindset behind an action.

examples.jp: 昨日は勉強するつもりだったが、寝てしまった。
examples.en: I had meant to study yesterday, but I fell asleep.

examples.jp: 冗談のつもりで言ったのに、彼は怒ってしまった。
examples.en: I said it as a joke, but he got angry.

20.summary: つもりだった voices an unfulfilled past plan, while つもりで names the intention or attitude behind an act.
20.details:
昨日は**勉強するつもりだった**が、寝てしまった。 *(I intended to study, but slept.)*

With a noun, Nのつもりで: 'on the assumption that / as if'. This differs from 予定だった, which suggests a scheduled plan.

21.title: 〜もせずに
21.structure: Verb (ます stem) + もせずに
21.explanation: An archaic or formal expression meaning 'not doing something that one would naturally expect to be done.' It emphasizes the lack of an expected action.

examples.jp: 父は具合が悪いのに、医者に行きもせずに仕事を続けている。
examples.en: Even though my father doesn't feel very well, he won't even go to see a doctor but just carries on working.

examples.jp: 彼は上司の許可を得もせずに、新しいプロジェクトを進めた。
examples.en: He went ahead with a new project without even getting permission from his boss.

21.summary: もせずに is a formal/literary way to emphasize that an action one would normally expect simply wasn't done — 'without even doing...'
21.details:
父は具合が悪いのに、医者に行き**もせずに**仕事を続けている。
*(Even though my father doesn't feel well, he won't even go see a doctor, and just keeps working.)*
彼は上司の許可を得**もせずに**、新しいプロジェクトを進めた。
*(He went ahead with a new project without even getting his boss's permission.)*

Formed from ます-stem + も + せずに (せずに being the formal negative of する, see Lesson 10-1's ずに) — the inserted も adds emphasis: "didn't even do the bare minimum you'd expect." This reads as more literary/formal than a plain ないで／ずに negative.

21.title: 〜かける／〜かけの
21.structure: V ます-stem + かける／かけの + N
21.explanation: An action was started but not finished, or is about to start.

examples.jp: 読みかけの本が机の上にある。
examples.en: There is a half-read book on the desk.

examples.jp: 彼は何か言いかけて、やめた。
examples.en: He started to say something and then stopped.

21.summary: かける marks an interrupted or just-begun action; the noun form かけの describes unfinished items.
21.details:
**読みかけの**本が机の上にある。 *(A half-read book is on the desk.)*

Compare 〜始める (begin and continue) and 〜終わる (finish). かける leaves the action in an incomplete state.

21.title: 〜込む
21.explanation: A compound-verb suffix meaning to go in, to do something deeply or thoroughly.

examples.jp: 彼は電車に乗り込んだ。
examples.en: He got on the train.

examples.jp: この資料をしっかり読み込んでおいてください。
examples.en: Please read this material thoroughly beforehand.

21.summary: 込む adds a sense of 'into' or 'deeply', as in 乗り込む、思い込む、読み込む.
21.details:
彼は電車に**乗り込んだ**。 *(He boarded the train.)*

Many 〜込む verbs are lexicalized (思い込む = be convinced; 話し込む = talk at length), so learn them as vocabulary as well.

21.title: 〜直す
21.explanation: Do something again to correct or improve it, not just repeat it.

examples.jp: 間違えたので、もう一度書き直します。
examples.en: I made a mistake, so I'll rewrite it.

examples.jp: 最初からやり直したい。
examples.en: I want to start over from the beginning.

21.summary: 直す after a verb stem means redoing it to fix or improve it.
21.details:
間違えたので、もう一度**書き直します**。 *(I'll write it again to fix the mistake.)*

Compare simply doing it once more with もう一度. Common: 見直す、考え直す、やり直す、作り直す.

21.title: 〜合う
21.explanation: An action done mutually between two or more people, or done together.

examples.jp: 二人はお互いに助け合って暮らしている。
examples.en: The two of them live helping each other.

examples.jp: みんなで話し合って、決めましょう。
examples.en: Let's talk it over together and decide.

21.summary: 合う signals reciprocity or joint action: 話し合う、助け合う、愛し合う.
21.details:
二人は**助け合って**暮らしている。 *(They live helping each other.)*

The subject needs to be plural or at least two parties. Not every 〜合う compound is reciprocal (似合う = suit).

21.title: 〜そうもない／〜そうにない
21.meaning: Doesn't look like it will ~ / Unlikely to ~
21.structure: V ます-stem + そうもない／そうにない
21.explanation: Judging from the situation, something seems unlikely to happen.

examples.jp: 今日は仕事が終わりそうにない。
examples.en: It doesn't look like I'll finish work today.

examples.jp: 雨はやみそうもない。
examples.en: The rain doesn't look like stopping.

21.summary: そうもない／そうにない is the negative guess 'doesn't seem likely to'.
21.details:
今日は仕事が**終わりそうにない**。 *(I can't see finishing today.)*

そうもない is a little more emphatic than そうにない. The plain negative そうではない/なさそうだ instead describes how something looks, not likelihood.

21.title: ところが
21.explanation: Introduces something that turned out contrary to what was expected from the previous sentence.

examples.jp: 道は空いていると思った。ところが、大渋滞だった。
examples.en: I thought the roads would be clear. But it turned out to be a huge traffic jam.

examples.jp: 試験は簡単だと聞いた。ところが、とても難しかった。
examples.en: I'd heard the exam was easy, but it was very difficult.

21.summary: ところが signals a surprising turn: reality differs from what the first sentence led one to expect.
21.details:
道は空いていると思った。**ところが**、大渋滞だった。 *(I thought it'd be clear. Yet it was jammed.)*

The following clause reports a past fact (never a command or wish). Compare しかし (plain contrast) and ところで (changing the subject).

22.title: 〜向け／〜向き
22.explanation: 向け shows who a product or service is aimed at. 向き shows suitability or orientation.

examples.jp: これは子供向けのアニメです。
examples.en: This is an anime aimed at children.

examples.jp: この仕事は彼に向いている。
examples.en: This job suits him.

22.summary: 向け = target audience (made for X); 向き = good fit for X.
22.details:
これは**子供向け**のアニメです。 *(This is an anime made for children.)*

この部屋は**家族向き**だ。 *(This room suits families.)*

The verb 向く (be suited) goes with に: 〜に向いている. 向け implies a deliberate target; 向き is a natural fit.

22.title: 〜上げる
22.explanation: Completing an action fully or raising it to a finished product.

examples.jp: 彼は三日で論文を書き上げた。
examples.en: He completed his thesis in three days.

examples.jp: ロボットを一人で作り上げた。
examples.en: He built the robot all by himself.

22.summary: 上げる as a suffix means finishing something through to the end, often a significant effort.
22.details:
彼は三日で論文を**書き上げた**。 *(He finished writing the thesis in three days.)*

Compare 〜終わる (plain finish) and 〜きる (do completely). 〜上げる gives a sense of achievement. Other uses are literal: 持ち上げる (lift).

22.title: 〜通す
22.meaning: Keep ~ing until the end / See through
22.explanation: Keep doing the same thing without stopping, through a period or despite difficulty.

examples.jp: 彼は最後まで自分の意見を言い通した。
examples.en: He stuck to his opinion to the very end.

examples.jp: 徹夜で勉強をやり通した。
examples.en: I carried through my studying all night.

22.summary: 通す means persisting in an action from start to finish.
22.details:
彼は最後まで**言い通した**。 *(He kept saying it to the very end.)*

It implies stubbornness or perseverance. Common compounds: 貫き通す、やり通す、頑張り通す.

22.title: 〜とは限らない
22.structure: Plain form + とは限らない
22.explanation: Denies a generalization, saying exceptions exist. The generalization is typically a common assumption.

examples.jp: 高いものが必ずしもいいとは限らない。
examples.en: Expensive things are not necessarily good.

examples.jp: 金持ちが幸せだとは限らない。
examples.en: Rich people aren't always happy.

22.summary: とは限らない weakens an overgeneralization: 'it is not always the case that ~'.
22.details:
高いものが**必ずしもいいとは限らない**。 *(Expensive isn't always better.)*

Often with 必ずしも or 全部が. It is a partial negation, so it doesn't mean the opposite is always true.

22.title: 〜たものだ
22.explanation: Recalls a habitual action in the past with a feeling of nostalgia.

examples.jp: 子供のころ、よくこの川で遊んだものだ。
examples.en: As a child, I used to play in this river a lot.

examples.jp: 学生時代は夜遅くまで友達と話したものです。
examples.en: In my student days we would talk with friends late into the night.

22.summary: たものだ looks back at a repeated past action with sentimental feeling.
22.details:
子供のころ、よく**遊んだものだ**。 *(I used to play there often as a child.)*

Often with よく or 昔は. Unlike 〜ていた (neutral description), it implies the speaker feels fondly about the memory.

22.title: とても〜ない
22.explanation: Emphasizes that something is impossible, however one tries. Common with potential verbs.

examples.jp: こんなに高い車は、とても買えない。
examples.en: I could never afford such an expensive car.

examples.jp: 彼の気持ちはとても理解できない。
examples.en: I can't possibly understand how he feels.

22.summary: とても + negative says 'there's no way I can ~', a stronger form of 'not able to'.
22.details:
こんなに高い車は、**とても買えない**。 *(There's no way I can buy such a car.)*

With an affirmative adjective, とても means 'very' (とても高い). The negative potential makes it an impossibility statement.

22.title: 〜一度に
22.meaning: At once / All at one time
22.explanation: Several things are done at the same moment or in a single go.

examples.jp: 一度にたくさんのことはできません。
examples.en: I can't do many things at once.

examples.jp: 荷物を一度に運ぶのは大変だ。
examples.en: It's hard to carry the luggage all at once.

22.summary: 一度に stresses doing multiple things or a large quantity in one go.
22.details:
荷物を**一度に**運ぶのは大変だ。 *(Carrying the luggage all at once is hard.)*

Compare 同時に (at the same time, for events or aspects) and まとめて (in bulk).

22.title: せいぜい
22.explanation: Sets an upper limit: even in the best case it won't exceed this. Often slightly disparaging.

examples.jp: この仕事は、せいぜい二時間で終わるよ。
examples.en: This job will take at most two hours.

examples.jp: 私にできるのは、せいぜいこの程度です。
examples.en: The most I can do is about this much.

22.summary: せいぜい marks an upper limit: 'at most', 'at best'.
22.details:
この仕事は、**せいぜい二時間**で終わるよ。 *(That job takes two hours at most.)*

Also used as encouragement 'do your best' in せいぜい頑張って, with an ironic tone. Use 多くても for a neutral 'at most'.

23.title: 〜可能性がある
23.structure: Plain form + 可能性がある
23.explanation: Means 'Pが起きる可能性がある' (there is a possibility that P will occur or is true). Used similarly to English.

examples.jp: あの学生は基礎的な学力があるし、努力家だから、これから大きく伸びる可能性がある。
examples.en: That student has basic academic ability and is a hard worker, so he has the potential to develop greatly in the future.

examples.jp: 携帯電話は非常に便利だが、場所によってはかからなくなる可能性もある。
examples.en: Mobiles are very handy, but it is also possible that they will not work in certain locations.

23.summary: 可能性がある states that there's a possibility something will happen or is true — functioning much like its literal English translation.
23.details:
あの学生は基礎的な学力があるし、努力家だから、これから大きく伸びる**可能性がある**。
*(That student has basic academic ability and is hard-working, so he has the potential to develop greatly.)*
携帯電話は非常に便利だが、場所によってはかからなくなる**可能性もある**。
*(Mobiles are handy, but there's also a possibility they won't work in certain locations.)*

Because 可能性 is a regular noun ("possibility"), this pattern behaves exactly as you'd expect from English — plain form + 可能性がある/もある — and doesn't carry any of the certainty-scale nuance that はずだ, に違いない, or かもしれない do (see Lesson 18-1's comparison of those).

23.title: 〜てごらん
23.meaning: Try ~ing (to a child or close person)
23.explanation: A gentle command encouraging someone to try. Used by adults to children or among close family.

examples.jp: ほら、これを食べてごらん。おいしいよ。
examples.en: Here, try eating this. It's tasty.

examples.jp: 自分でやってごらん。
examples.en: Try doing it by yourself.

23.summary: てごらん is the soft, friendly 'give it a try' used downwards or among intimates.
23.details:
ほら、これを**食べてごらん**。 *(Here, try this.)*

It comes from ご覧になる; with a stranger or superior, use てみてください. Do not use it toward people of higher status.

23.title: 〜のでしょうか
23.meaning: I wonder if ~ / Is it that ~?
23.structure: Plain form + のでしょうか
23.explanation: A polite question that seeks explanation or confirmation, softer and more tentative than か.

examples.jp: この荷物はどこに置けばいいのでしょうか。
examples.en: Where should I put this luggage?

examples.jp: 本当にこれで大丈夫なのでしょうか。
examples.en: I wonder whether this is really okay.

23.summary: のでしょうか is a polite, careful question that invites an explanation.
23.details:
この荷物は**どこに置けばいいのでしょうか**。 *(Where would be best to put this?)*

The の explains a situation, and でしょうか softens it. You can also think aloud with it: ~のだろうか (written/inner voice).

23.title: 〜っけ
23.explanation: Used when you are trying to remember something you once knew, confirming it with yourself or someone.

examples.jp: 明日の会議、何時からだっけ？
examples.en: What time was tomorrow's meeting again?

examples.jp: あれ、この人の名前は何だったっけ。
examples.en: Hmm, what was this person's name again?

23.summary: っけ marks a half-remembered fact the speaker wants to confirm.
23.details:
明日の会議、**何時からだっけ**？ *(What time is the meeting again?)*

Casual only. It can refer to the past (だったっけ) or present, and sounds like thinking aloud, so don't use it with someone you must be polite to.

23.title: 〜か何か
23.explanation: Gives an example while suggesting other similar possibilities, to avoid being specific.

examples.jp: お茶か何か飲みませんか。
examples.en: Shall we have tea or something?

examples.jp: 病気か何かで、休んでいるのだろう。
examples.en: He's probably off because of illness or something.

23.summary: か何か softens a statement by naming one example and hinting at others.
23.details:
**お茶か何か**飲みませんか。 *(How about tea or something?)*

The vagueness is polite and casual. Similar to とか and など, but か何か offers the example as one choice among alternatives.

23.title: 〜において／〜における
23.structure: Noun + において／における + Noun
23.explanation: A formal way of saying で (location, time or field). における modifies a following noun.

examples.jp: 会議は東京において開かれた。
examples.en: The meeting was held in Tokyo.

examples.jp: 日本における英語教育の問題を考える。
examples.en: We consider problems with English education in Japan.

23.summary: において／における mark a formal setting (place, time, field), replacing で and での.
23.details:
会議は**東京において**開かれた。 *(The meeting took place in Tokyo.)*

**日本における**英語教育 *(English education in Japan)*

Use in speeches, reports and formal writing; in conversation で is natural.

23.title: 〜よりも
23.explanation: Emphasized form of より in comparisons, often placing the contrast at the front.

examples.jp: お金よりも、健康のほうが大切です。
examples.en: Health is more important than money.

examples.jp: 予想していたよりも、ずっと簡単だった。
examples.en: It was much easier than I had expected.

23.summary: よりも is the emphatic comparison particle, with the same logic as より.
23.details:
**お金よりも**、健康のほうが大切です。 *(Health matters more than money.)*

も adds emphasis or allows the phrase to be fronted. It can also follow a clause (予想していたよりも).

23.title: 〜結果
23.structure: V た-form / N の + 結果、〜
23.explanation: States the outcome that came after a process of doing something, usually after a long effort or deliberation.

examples.jp: よく考えた結果、会社を辞めることにした。
examples.en: After careful thought, I decided to quit my job.

examples.jp: 調査の結果、原因が分かった。
examples.en: As a result of the investigation, the cause was found.

23.summary: 結果 links a completed process to its outcome, as in 検討した結果.
23.details:
**よく考えた結果**、会社を辞めることにした。 *(After careful thought, I decided to quit.)*

The preceding verb is a deliberate action. The outcome clause is a past decision, discovery or result. Compare 〜上で (after ~ as a prerequisite).

24.title: V-ます ＋ きる
24.explanation: Means '完全に〜する' (do completely) or, with motion verbs, '最初から最後まで〜する' (do from beginning to end).

examples.jp: 彼はマラソンで42.195kmを走りきった。
examples.en: He completed (ran the entire distance) 42.195 km in the marathon.

examples.jp: 山本さんは疲れきった顔で座り込んでいる。
examples.en: Mr. Yamamoto is slumped in a chair looking completely exhausted.

24.summary: ます-stem + きる means doing something completely, or from beginning to end without stopping — often used with verbs of exertion or motion.
24.details:
彼はマラソンで42.195kmを**走りきった**。 *(He ran the entire 42.195 km marathon distance.)*
山本さんは**疲れきった**顔で座り込んでいる。 *(Mr. Yamamoto is slumped in a chair, looking utterly exhausted.)*

きり attaches to the ます-stem and conveys either "did it completely/thoroughly" (走りきる, 使いきる — "used it all up") or, with a state-verb like 疲れる, an intensified "completely/utterly" reading (疲れきった, "utterly exhausted," stronger than just 疲れた). Common with verbs of physical exertion where reaching the natural endpoint of an effort is the whole point.

24.title: 〜にしても
24.structure: Plain form / N + にしても
24.explanation: Accepts a premise for argument's sake, but the main clause still holds or contradicts expectation.

examples.jp: 忙しいにしても、連絡くらいはできるはずだ。
examples.en: Even granting that you're busy, you could at least get in touch.

examples.jp: 冗談にしても、言い過ぎだ。
examples.en: Even if it was a joke, you went too far.

24.summary: にしても concedes a point and then states that the conclusion stands anyway.
24.details:
**忙しいにしても**、連絡くらいはできるはずだ。 *(Busy or not, you could contact me.)*

The pattern is close to としても and にしろ/にせよ (more formal). Nouns can attach directly: 冗談にしても.

24.title: 〜的（てき）
24.explanation: A suffix that turns a noun into a な-adjective describing a quality, aspect or attitude.

examples.jp: 彼は積極的に意見を言う。
examples.en: He actively expresses his opinions.

examples.jp: それは一般的な考え方ではない。
examples.en: That isn't a common way of thinking.

24.summary: 的 creates adjectives from nouns (積極的、具体的、一般的) and works as な-adjective / adverb with に.
24.details:
彼は**積極的に**意見を言う。 *(He expresses opinions actively.)*

的 words take な before a noun and に before a verb. Not every noun accepts 的, so learn the common ones (基本的、個人的、国際的).

24.title: 〜は別として
24.explanation: Excludes one case from consideration while making a statement about the rest.

examples.jp: 冗談は別として、本当に困っているんだ。
examples.en: Joking aside, I'm really in trouble.

examples.jp: 値段は別として、品質は最高だ。
examples.en: Price aside, the quality is top-notch.

24.summary: は別として sets one factor aside to discuss the others.
24.details:
**冗談は別として**、本当に困っているんだ。 *(Joking aside, I'm in real trouble.)*

The set-aside element appears before は別として; it works like 〜はともかく.

24.title: 〜は〜で有名
24.structure: N1 は N2 で有名だ
24.explanation: Says that something or someone is well known for a particular feature.

examples.jp: 京都は古いお寺で有名です。
examples.en: Kyoto is famous for its old temples.

examples.jp: この店はラーメンで有名だ。
examples.en: This shop is famous for its ramen.

24.summary: AはBで有名だ names what A is known for.
24.details:
京都は**古いお寺で有名**です。 *(Kyoto is known for its old temples.)*

When the thing being known for is a person's career, use として有名: 彼は作家として有名だ. で marks the feature, として the role.

24.title: すなわち
24.meaning: That is / Namely / In other words
24.explanation: Rephrases the first term with an exact equivalent, in formal writing.

examples.jp: 日本の首都、すなわち東京は人口が多い。
examples.en: Japan's capital, namely Tokyo, has a large population.

examples.jp: 彼は私の父の兄、すなわち伯父です。
examples.en: He is my father's elder brother, that is, my uncle.

24.summary: すなわち gives an exact equivalent or definition, a formal alternative to つまり.
24.details:
日本の首都、**すなわち**東京は人口が多い。 *(The capital, that is Tokyo, is heavily populated.)*

つまり can summarize or conclude, but すなわち strictly identifies two terms that mean the same.

24.title: 例えば
24.explanation: Introduces a concrete example of what was just said.

examples.jp: 日本には、例えば京都のような古い町があります。
examples.en: Japan has old towns like, for example, Kyoto.

examples.jp: 例えば、毎日十分歩くだけでも体にいいです。
examples.en: For example, just walking ten minutes a day is good for you.

24.summary: 例えば introduces an illustration, often followed by のような or など.
24.details:
日本には、**例えば**京都のような古い町があります。 *(Japan has old towns, for example Kyoto.)*

例えば is often written in hiragana (たとえば). Don't confuse it with たとえ〜ても (even if).

24.title: 確かに
24.structure: 確かに + clause + が／けど、〜
24.explanation: Agrees with a point (or states it firmly) before adding a contrast or reservation.

examples.jp: 確かにこの方法は安いが、時間がかかる。
examples.en: It's true that this method is cheap, but it takes time.

examples.jp: 確かに、彼の言うとおりだ。
examples.en: You're right, it's just as he says.

24.summary: 確かに concedes a fact and often sets up a 'but' that follows.
24.details:
**確かに**この方法は安い**が**、時間がかかる。 *(Admittedly it's cheap, but it takes time.)*

Often used in debate, 確かに〜が、〜 grants the other side's point. By itself, 確かに works as 'indeed'.

24.title: 〜てもしょうがない／〜てもしかたがない
24.meaning: It's no use ~ing / There's no helping ~
24.structure: V て-form + もしょうがない／もしかたがない
24.explanation: Even if you do something, it won't change anything, so you may as well accept things.

examples.jp: 今さら悔やんでもしょうがない。
examples.en: There's no use regretting it now.

examples.jp: 怒ってもしかたがないよ。
examples.en: There's no point in getting angry.

24.summary: てもしょうがない accepts a situation as unchangeable, so effort or emotion is wasted.
24.details:
今さら**悔やんでもしょうがない**。 *(Regret is pointless now.)*

しかたがない is a little more formal than しょうがない. Compare ても始まらない with the same meaning, and てしょうがない (can't help feeling).
